mainEntity.name: Is a garage conversion better than building a new ground-up addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Converting an attached garage into living space is often faster and less disruptive than building a traditional ground-up addition because the exterior walls, roof, and concrete slab already exist. However, the tradeoff is losing vehicle parking and storage. A garage conversion also requires raising or leveling the floor, adding comprehensive insulation, upgrading electrical circuits, and extending HVAC ductwork or installing a mini-split system. A new ground-up addition costs more initially but preserves vehicle storage while delivering fully customized layout dimensions.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion uses existing framing to save on construction time and structural costs, but you give up covered parking and must upgrade floor grading, insulation, and HVAC.
